title: BoJ Tankan (March 2027 survey) — 08:50 JST, the first business day of the new Japanese fiscal year
source: EST: boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/tkohyos.xlsx ('Schedule for Releases of Statistical Data (From July 2026 to June 2027)'), re-fetched direct 2027-04-01-relevant row on 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 48,500 bytes, md5 d03654377cb5188caa65d1d5f1b73533 — byte-identical to the 2026-09-05 fetch recorded on boj-tankan-2026-10-01) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its 'Statistics data' sheet during the boj-tankan-2026-10-01 pulse-check adjacency sweep. Row 230 gives the Mar.-Survey column of 'Tankan (Short-Term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) / Summary and Outline' at '8:50 a.m.'; row 231 gives that column's date as Excel serial 46478 = 2027-04-01. The serial decoding is validated against an observed release on the same row: its June-survey cell is serial 46204 = 2026-07-01, which matches the June 2026 survey's already-published release date on the Bank's own archive (boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/gaiyo/2026/index.htm, HTTP 200, re-read 2026-09-15, reading 'July 1, 2026'). Rows 233/235 put the Comprehensive Data Set and Long-Term Time-Series Data at serial 46479 = 2027-04-02, 'Around 8:50 a.m.' Release time corroborated verbatim from the Bank's methodology page boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/exp/tk/extk.htm: 'The survey results are released at the beginning of April, July, October, and mid-December in principle (released at 8:50 a.m. Japan Standard Time).' Filed estimate on two counts, identical to the fourteen BoJ entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: for the Federal Reserve and no slot for the Bank of Japan, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Note the schedule workbook itself covers July 2026 - June 2027 only and the Bank republishes it each June and December, so this date should be re-verified against the successor workbook once it publishes.
notes: PROPOSED during the boj-tankan-2026-10-01 interval-elapsed pulse (2026-09-15, D-16) and owned by that lane, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md's one-file-per-owner rule (#1717). Discovered as a by-product of re-running that ledger's registered date kill switch against the primary rather than from a separate hunt: the same workbook row that fixes 2026-10-01 (serial 46296) and 2026-12-14 (serial 46370) also fixes 2027-04-01 (serial 46478), and the calendar carried the first two and not the third. Filed for one specific reason beyond series completeness: 2027-04-01 is ALREADY a tracked date on this calendar (japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01, the 8%-to-1% food consumption-tax cut taking effect), so the March 2027 Tankan collides with a mechanical Japanese CPI event on the first business day of the new fiscal year. That is a denser Tokyo bar than any Tankan this calendar currently tracks, and it is exactly the sort of collision the boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-10-01 lane filed boj-tankan-2026-10-01 to study. Impact is MEDIUM, matching boj-tankan-2026-10-01 and one tier above every BoJ meeting-account entry, for the same reason that entry gives: the Tankan is a first-release statistical print under the Statistics Law over a ~210,000-firm population with a genuine surprise component, not an anonymised digest of an already-reported meeting. It is not raised above MEDIUM because symbols is empty, no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed, and the channel to this book's AI names runs through yen funding and global term premium, both second-order and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers. What the proposing ledger's own research says the eventual researcher should NOT assume: boj-tankan-2026-10-01 measured the Tankan's Nikkei opening-gap elevation at 0.88x an ordinary session over the Bank's full published history of 90 releases (2004-2026), against the 1.28x a 2016+ window had shown, and found the release's own published surprise uncorrelated with the gap (Spearman +0.173, permutation p = 0.440). March surveys are also perfectly collinear with the quarter's first trading day, so this instance inherits the same identification limit the Apr/Jul/Oct cohort carries; the mid-December survey remains the one structurally clean cut.
